S29.27.needs: a Free or paid account; the run may ask for approval first (plan requirement not verified in the code); a phone or Mac with the app signed in
S29.27.note: The plan's line numbers were stale; the feature was found in CodeExecutionBlock.tsx, MessageBubble.tsx (renders it) and CodeRunAgain.tsx. Chart display under the output was not traced to a visible label, and the entry route into the panel depends on the model deciding to run code, so the exact words in the reply are not known.
steps: Sign in and open a chat on the main chat screen.
Send a request that needs Python, for example: "Using this small table of numbers I type, calculate the average and draw a chart in Python." Type the numbers in the message.
Wait for the reply. Look for the block titled "Code Execution" under the reply; it shows "Running Python…" while it runs.
Tap the "Code Execution" block to expand it and check that the "Output" heading shows the printed result.

Look for the code the run used (its code card in the tool row) and for any chart drawn below the output, and compare with Expected: code, output and charts all visible. Optionally tap "Run again" to repeat the run.
S29.27.where: Chat screen > send a message asking for Python analysis of some data > under the assistant's reply, the block titled "Code Execution" (status "Running Python…"); tap it to expand "Output"; the run's code is in the tool row, where "Run again" re-runs it

S29.35.needs: a signed-in account and a chat that contains a table; a phone or Mac to see the share sheet
S29.35.note: The plan's line 394 moved; the table download control is now at MessageContentRenderer.tsx lines 373-379 and 438-442. The CSV download is also present in the spreadsheet viewer as "Share as CSV".
steps: Sign in and open a chat where the assistant has returned a table (ask for a small table, e.g. "make a table of 3 fruits and their prices").
Find the table's action buttons in the table header area and tap the one labeled "Download table as CSV".
Check that the share sheet opens with a file ending in .csv (the file name is built from the table title or "table").
Optional route: open a CSV file artifact and tap the icon labeled "Share as CSV", then check the share sheet and that a .csv file is offered.
S29.35.where: Chat screen > an assistant answer that contains a table > tap the table's "Download table as CSV" button (an icon; its label is that text), then the share sheet opens. Or open a CSV/spreadsheet file in the answer's artifact view and tap the share icon labeled "Share as CSV"

S29.36.needs: a signed-in account and a chat answer that contains a chart; a phone or Mac to see the share sheet
S29.36.note: The plan's line numbers were stale; the export is at ReportChart.tsx lines 817-836 and the button at 910-924, and it calls exportPngImage in apps/mobile/services/fileCreation.ts. The only export is a PNG image, not a data file.
steps: Sign in and open a chat where the assistant returns a chart (ask for a simple bar or line chart of a few values).
Look at the chart's footer row for the buttons "Show data" and "Save image".
Tap "Save image"; the label changes to "Saving…" while it works, then the share sheet opens with a PNG picture of the chart.
If saving fails, check that the alert "Could not save the chart" appears instead of a share sheet.
Compare with Expected: the user can export the chart as an image file. Tap "Show data" to confirm the table of values is also visible.
S29.36.where: Chat screen > an assistant answer that shows a chart > tap "Show data" to see the numbers, and tap "Save image" at the bottom of the chart to save it as a picture through the share sheet
